1.title: Variables, Outputs, Locals and Complex Types
1.text: Welcome to Module six: Variables, Outputs, Locals and Complex Types. It covers the exam area four. Terraform configuration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. four C Use variables and outputs. four D Understand and use complex types. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four. Terraform configuration. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: Input variables
1.text: Input variables. Input variables make a configuration reusable: they are the parameters of a module or of the root configuration. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Input variables, continued
1.text: Input variables. type. The allowed type (string, number, bool, list, map, object and so on). default. The value used if none is given; without a default the variable is required. description. Documentation for users. sensitive. Hide the value in C L I output (Module ten). nullable. Whether null is allowed. validation. Custom rules (Module nine). How values are supplied, from lowest to highest precedence.

1.title: Input variables, continued
1.text: Input variables. one (lowest). Default in the variable block. two. Environment variables named T F var name. three. terraform dot tfvars and terraform dot tfvars dot json. four. dot auto dot tfvars and dot auto dot tfvars dot json (alphabetical order). five (highest). -var and -var file on the command line (in the order given). If a required variable has no value anywhere, Terraform asks for it interactively. Exam tip: Command-line -var and -var file win over everything. T F var name is an environment variable. No default means the variable is required.

1.title: Output values
1.text: Output values. Outputs expose information from a configuration: to the user after apply, or to a parent module or another configuration. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Output values, continued
1.text: Output values. Shown after apply. Root module outputs are printed. terraform output. Reads outputs from the state; terraform output -json for scripts. sensitive true. Hides the value in output. In a child module. An output is the only way the parent can read a value (Module twelve).

1.title: Local values
1.text: Local values. Locals name an expression so you can reuse it and avoid repetition. They are not inputs: callers cannot set them. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Local values, continued
1.text: Local values. Reference with local dot name prefix (singular local ). Exam tip: Variables are inputs; locals are internal names; outputs are results. The block is locals, the reference is local..

1.title: Types and complex types
1.text: Types and complex types. Primitive. Type: string. Example: web. Type: number. Example: three. Type: bool. Example: true. Collection. Type: list type. Example: Ordered, allows duplicates: a, b. Type: set type. Example: Unordered, unique values. Type: map type. Example: Keys to values of one type: a one, b two. Structural. Type: tuple... Example: Ordered, each element its own type. Type: object... Example: Named attributes with their own types. Special. Type: any. Example: Let Terraform decide the type.

1.title: Types and complex types, continued
1.text: Types and complex types. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: List equals ordered, set equals unique and unordered, map equals keys and values of one type, object equals named attributes of different types. A type constraint makes Terraform convert or reject wrong values.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A variable block has no default value and the user supplies none. What does Terraform do on plan? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Asks the user for the value. A required variable with no value is requested interactively.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which source of a variable value has the highest precedence? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The -var option on the command line. Command-line -var and -var-file override all other sources.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. How is the value of a local named name prefix referenced? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: local.name prefix. Locals are defined in a locals block and referenced with the singular prefix local.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which type holds unique values with no order? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: set. A set holds unique values and has no order; a list is ordered and may repeat values.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A child module must give its parent the I D of a network it creates. What should the module declare? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: An output block with the I D. Outputs are the only way a parent module can read values from a child module.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which command shows the output values stored in the state? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: terraform output. terraform output reads the output values from the state.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What makes an input variable required? Answer: Having no default value. Question two. What is the name of an environment variable for a variable called region? Answer: T F var region. Question three. What do outputs expose? Answer: Values to the user or to a parent module.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the difference between list and set? Answer: A list is ordered and may repeat; a set is unique and unordered. Question five. What type has named attributes of different types? Answer: object. Question six. How do you reference a local value? Answer: local.N A M E.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Variables: type, default, description, sensitive, validation; no default equals required. Precedence: default, T F var, tfvars, auto.tfvars, -var and -var-file (highest). Outputs: expose values; terraform output; child module outputs reach the parent. Locals: named expressions; local.N A M E. Types: string, number, bool; list, set, map; tuple, object; any.
